html:
A school of Zen Buddhism brought to Japan from Song China by the monk Eisai, who returned in 1191. It shaped much of samurai culture and the arts of medieval Japan.

Rinzai comes from Linji, a Chinese Chan master of the 800s. Its training stresses sitting meditation and the koan, a puzzling question or story that a student works on until the mind breaks through ordinary thinking. Eisai also brought tea seeds and wrote a book praising tea for health, which helped spread tea drinking in Japan.

He found patrons in the new warrior government of the Kamakura shogunate. Later shoguns ranked the great Zen temples of Kamakura and Kyoto in an official system, the Five Mountains. Zen monks served as advisers, diplomats and teachers of Chinese learning.

Through these temples Rinzai Zen influenced ink painting, rock gardens, Noh theatre, and the tea ceremony refined by Sen no Rikyū. A second Zen school, Sōtō, was brought from China by Dōgen in 1227.
sum: A school of Zen Buddhism brought to Japan from Song China by the monk Eisai, who returned in 1191. It shaped much of samurai culture and the arts of medieval Japan.
